memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'You will eat the flesh of your sons and the flesh of your daughters. I
will destroy your high places, cut down your incense altars and pile your
dead bodies on the lifeless forms of your idols, and I will abhor you'"
- Lev 26:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is perhaps the most horrifying verse in the chapter, and we must not
soften it or skip past it. It describes the extremity of famine under
siege, and the total collapse of a society that has abandoned God. Tragically,
Scripture records that such horrors did occur during later sieges of
Jerusalem (Lam 4:10).

Why would God include such a terrible warning? Because love tells the
truth about where a road leads, even when the truth is dreadful. God was
showing His people the full horror at the end of the path of persistent
rebellion — not to terrify them for its own sake, but to turn them back
before they ever reached it.

Notice what stood at the centre of it all: the idols. God says He will
pile the dead bodies on the lifeless forms of the idols they trusted.
There is a bitter irony here. The false gods they turned to for life could
only preside over death.

Dear reader, this is what idolatry ultimately delivers. Every false god
we chase — whether carved stone or career, pleasure or pride — promises
life and finally presides over ruin. Sin always pays wages, and Paul names
them plainly: the wages of sin is death (Rom 6:23).

But that same verse does not end there: the gift of God is eternal life in
Christ Jesus our Lord. The horror of where sin leads makes the rescue of
the cross shine all the brighter.

Flee to Christ, who leads to life, not to the idols that preside over
death.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What false gods have I trusted that can only lead to emptiness?
2. Have I taken seriously where sin ultimately leads?
3. How does the horror of sin make Christ's rescue more precious to me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You for telling me the truth about where rebellion leads.
Turn me from every idol that promises life but delivers death, and lead me
to Christ, who gives true life. Amen.
